_doc: What raw openFDA FAERS actually throws at the pipeline — the mess the trust layer (bullet 1) conquers. Profiled from 3,000 raw adverse-event reports BEFORE any cleaning. This is the evidence behind 'no matter how messy the data comes in, it never mixes with the good'.

nested_json_depth.why_hard: deeply nested patient/drug/openfda/reaction objects — not flat rows; must be parsed + flattened

null_drug_name_pct.why_hard: openfda.generic_name missing on 1 in 7 drugs; a naive join loses them

list_valued_reactions.why_hard: non-atomic / multi-valued — breaks a flat star; requires a many-to-many bridge

missing_country_pct.why_hard: occurcountry absent on 57 reports — nullable dimension key

ragged_schema.value: 27 top-level fields, 3 present in <90% of records
ragged_schema.why_hard: sparse/inconsistent fields per record — no fixed shape

what_the_trust_layer_does.list_valued_reactions: explode into bridge_report_reaction (8,232 links) -> dim_reaction (1,828) — M2M done right, not dropped
what_the_trust_layer_does.nested_json: parse to a conformed event-grain fact_adverse_events (grain = safetyreportid)
what_the_trust_layer_does.missing_country: nullable handled; dim_country built from present values (44)
what_the_trust_layer_does.contract_enforcement: versioned data_contract.yml PASS/WARN/FAIL; FAIL-level rows route to quarantine, never silent-drop

claim_backed: bullet 1 (Data Quality) — 'however messy the data arrives, it never contaminates the clean layer'
